title: The Produce Stand
story:
On his eighty-fifth morning since leaving the Great Canopy, James woke early to the cool dampness of the cottonwood grove. After checking his small brass compass to confirm their heading, he and Nico set out along the treeline, keeping parallel to the highway where the morning fog was slowly lifting. The roar of early traffic vibrated through the earth, but here on the grassy margins, the path was soft underfoot. By mid-morning, the dense thicket opened up near a wide gravel turn-off where a bustling roadside produce market was coming to life.

James and Nico slipped behind a rustic split-rail wooden fence overgrown with climbing honeysuckle vines to observe. Below them, local farmers were unloading small, modern pickup trucks, hauling heavy wooden crates and woven wicker baskets toward shaded canvas stalls. The air smelled intoxicatingly rich—a mix of sweet crushed pineapples, ripe papayas, fresh earth, and lingering exhaust fumes. Reminded briefly of the quiet cedar shavings in Don Tadeo's workshop, James appreciated the stark contrast of this noisy, vibrant energy while remaining safely hidden in the leafy shade.

While James carefully surveyed the area from his high fence post, Nico's nose twitched uncontrollably. Driven by restless curiosity and the irresistible scent of sweet fruit, the little deer mouse scrambled down the wooden rail toward the gravel below. James chirped a low, urgent warning, but the noise of revving truck engines drowned out his voice. Nico darted across the gravel, weaving between the tires of a parked blue pickup truck where several large, covered wicker baskets sat piled on the lowered tailgate.

Disaster struck in an instant. Nico leaped into an open wicker basket filled with dried fruit chips just as a busy vendor stepped over. Without looking inside, the man slammed the hinged wooden lid shut, pushed a wooden locking peg into the latch, and lifted another heavy crate directly on top of it. James gasped from the fence line, his heart pounding in his chest as the truck driver climbed into the cab and turned the ignition key.
location: A split-rail wooden fence near a roadside produce stand south of San Antonio del Río
